$comment: Single source of truth for the two files that make Universal Links and App
Links work. Both are generated by build.mjs, which refuses to run while any
required value is missing — a wrong or placeholder value here does not fail
loudly, it makes links silently open the website instead of the app, which is
very hard to tell apart from 'the feature is not built yet'.
appleTeamId: App Store Connect, Membership Details, 10 characters.
androidSha256: the signing certificate fingerprint, colon-separated uppercase
hex. Get it from `eas credentials` once a build profile exists. It is the
*upload/app-signing* certificate, and Google Play re-signs by default, so for
any build distributed through Play use the fingerprint Play shows under
Setup > App integrity, not the local keystore's.
$variantsComment: production carries two fingerprints and both are load-bearing. The first is
the EAS upload keystore, which signs anything installed straight from EAS.
The second is the Google Play app-signing key (Play Console > Setup > App
integrity): Play strips the upload signature and re-signs with this key, so
it is the certificate every device that installed from the closed test
actually checks. Removing either silently breaks App Links for that install
preview's fingerprint arrived with the first preview build: EAS creates one
keystore per application identifier, on first use, so each variant has its own.
development still has none, because no development build has been made.
preview is distributed as an APK straight from EAS and is never re-signed, so
unlike production this one fingerprint is the whole story.
$pathsComment: Only routes that have an in-app equivalent are claimed. Claiming a path the
app cannot render means a tapped link opens the app and shows nothing, which
is worse than opening the browser. Everything else — the marketing page,
privacy, terms, and .well-known itself — must stay unclaimed.
Corrected 2026-08-19 with the invitation resolver: this said /list/* and the
route is app/lists/[id].tsx. The mismatch was silent in both directions and
is the exact failure the rule above describes — /list/x opened the app onto
+not-found, while /lists/x, the shape anything would actually generate, was
not claimed at all and opened Safari. Neither reads as a wrong path; both
read as the feature not working.
